events.title: Supreme Court strikes down IEEPA tariffs
events.why_it_matters: The 6-3 ruling invalidated the legal basis for Trump's broadest tariffs, forcing a chaotic reset of US trade policy and opening refund claims for importers.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the new Section 122 tariff survives legal challenge and how quickly refunds reach retailers.

events.title: Trump imposes new 15% global tariff under Section 122
events.why_it_matters: Within days of the Supreme Court loss, the administration re-imposed a universal tariff at 15%, keeping trade costs elevated and uncertainty high for importers.
events.what_to_watch: Implementation guidance, exempted product lists, and retaliation from major trading partners.

events.title: China Fifth Plenum concludes without major stimulus
events.why_it_matters: The plenum focused on party governance rather than a large consumption or property stimulus, disappointing cyclical bulls expecting a demand boost.
events.what_to_watch: Follow-through from the NDRC on already-announced incremental policies and the 15th Five-Year Plan framework.

events.title: US Q3 GDP advance estimate 3.4%
events.why_it_matters: Growth accelerated well above the 3.1% consensus, reinforcing the soft-landing narrative and reducing near-term recession odds.
events.what_to_watch: The second estimate on Nov 25 for revisions to consumer spending and investment.

events.title: US September PCE inflation 3.6% y/y, core 0.3% m/m
events.why_it_matters: Headline PCE accelerated to 3.6% and core matched expectations, keeping inflation uncomfortably above target and a December hike live.
events.what_to_watch: Whether October CPI on Nov 4 confirms sticky services inflation.

events.title: FOMC holds rates at 3.75%–4.00%, two dissents for a hike
events.why_it_matters: The Fed paused as widely expected, but two dissents preferring a 25bp hike signal the committee is not done tightening, keeping rate volatility elevated.
events.what_to_watch: Fed speeches next week for the December meeting odds and any hint on the balance sheet.

events.title: ECB holds rates unchanged
events.why_it_matters: The ECB paused amid weak growth and elevated energy-driven inflation, leaving the euro and European bonds data-dependent.
events.what_to_watch: Eurozone flash CPI and GDP revisions for the next policy signal.

events.title: Bank of Japan holds at 1.25%, one dissent, raises ETF purchase pace
events.why_it_matters: The BOJ held as expected but the dissent and ETF buying adjustment keep a December hike on the table, supporting yen volatility.
events.what_to_watch: Governor Ueda's guidance on wage-driven inflation and the next meeting in December.

events.title: France riots calm after worst unrest in years
events.why_it_matters: The violence has subsided but the political damage weakens the French government and reinforces ECB caution.
events.what_to_watch: Whether protests re-escalate around budget debates or pension reform.

events.title: Teck Highland Valley copper strike cuts supply
events.why_it_matters: A strike at a major Canadian copper mine is tightening concentrate supply, adding upside pressure to copper prices already supported by electrification demand.
events.what_to_watch: Negotiation progress and whether other copper operations face similar labour actions.

events.title: Iran/Hormuz tensions escalate; Brent above $115
events.why_it_matters: Reports of possible new US strikes on Iran and disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz are keeping a large geopolitical risk premium in oil, with Brent near $116.
events.what_to_watch: Any confirmed military action, Iranian retaliation, or closure of shipping lanes.

events.title: US sanctions relief for Russia continues via diesel deal
events.why_it_matters: Washington is selectively easing sanctions to allow Russian diesel imports, a potential bearish supply signal for oil products but a geopolitical gamble that could unsettle allies.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the EU follows or pushes back, and whether the deal expands to crude.

events.title: China restricts AI and chip-design technology exports
events.why_it_matters: Beijing added 23 AI technologies to its export-control list and imposed registration on outbound frontier models and chip IP, escalating tech fragmentation.
events.what_to_watch: Retaliation from the US and Taiwan and compliance costs for global semiconductor firms.

events.title: Taiwan tightens AI chip and server export controls to China
events.why_it_matters: Taipei criminalised unauthorised AI chip and server exports to China, aligning with US restrictions and adding compliance risk across the semiconductor supply chain.
events.what_to_watch: Enforcement actions and whether TSMC and other foundries face new licensing requirements.

events.title: OPEC+ monthly meeting
events.why_it_matters: The seven OPEC+ countries meet with Brent above $115; consensus expects a rollover of quotas, but any surprise cut would tighten an already nervous market.
events.what_to_watch: Compliance rhetoric from Saudi Arabia and Russia and whether the group acknowledges the Hormuz risk premium.

events.title: US ISM Manufacturing PMI for October
events.why_it_matters: Manufacturing has been hovering near expansion; a weak print would reinforce the two-speed US economy narrative ahead of the midterms.
events.what_to_watch: New orders and prices-paid sub-indices for tariff pass-through signals.

events.title: Apple FQ4 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Consensus expects ~$113.3B revenue and ~$1.98 EPS; a strong iPhone cycle could steady mega-cap tech after a volatile October.
events.what_to_watch: Gross margin guidance amid rising memory costs and commentary on the foldable iPhone pipeline.

events.title: US midterm elections
events.why_it_matters: Prediction markets price a Democratic House and a toss-up Senate; divided government would limit legislation but shift oversight and regulatory risk.
events.what_to_watch: Whether results are clear on election night or contested, and the sector implications for healthcare, energy and financials.

events.title: AMD Q3 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: AMD is a key AI and data-center bellwether; consensus EPS is ~$1.94, and guidance will frame the semiconductor outlook into 2027.
events.what_to_watch: MI-series GPU shipment commentary and whether AI capex is broadening beyond Nvidia.

events.title: US JOLTS job openings for September
events.why_it_matters: A further cooling in openings would support the Fed's pause, while resilience would keep a December hike in play.
events.what_to_watch: Quits rate and layoffs for signs of labour-market tightening or loosening.

events.title: US CPI for October
events.why_it_matters: With September CPI at 3.7%, October CPI is the last major inflation print before the December FOMC and could decide whether the Fed hikes again.
events.what_to_watch: Core services ex-housing and goods prices for tariff pass-through.

events.title: Qualcomm FQ4 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Qualcomm is a key smartphone and edge-AI supplier; consensus EPS is ~$1.46, and guidance will signal handset demand into the holiday season.
events.what_to_watch: Automotive and IoT growth versus handset weakness, and any China demand commentary.

events.title: Bank of England rate decision and Monetary Policy Report
events.why_it_matters: The BoE is expected to hold at 3.75% after the ECB pause; the vote split and new forecasts will shape GBP and gilt markets.
events.what_to_watch: Whether any MPC members vote for a cut and the inflation projection path.

events.title: US October employment report
events.why_it_matters: The jobs report is the last major labour-market data before the December FOMC; consensus expects payroll growth to cool but remain positive.
events.what_to_watch: Unemployment rate, average hourly earnings, and any strike-related distortions.

events.title: China October trade data
events.why_it_matters: Trade data will show whether export strength is offsetting weak domestic demand, a key signal for global cyclical sentiment.
events.what_to_watch: Export growth to the US and EU, and chip-related import volumes.

events.title: Anthropic IPO on Nasdaq
events.why_it_matters: A mega-cap AI IPO valued at up to $2T could either validate the AI trade or drain liquidity from existing tech names, making it a sentiment pivot.
events.what_to_watch: Final pricing, demand metrics, and first-day trading stability.

events.title: US PPI for October
events.why_it_matters: Producer prices will show whether tariff costs are feeding into pipeline inflation, a key input for the Fed's December decision.
events.what_to_watch: Core PPI and services margin trends.

events.title: Palantir Q3 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Palantir is a high-beta AI software bellwether; its commercial growth and government contract pipeline will be watched closely.
events.what_to_watch: US commercial customer additions and AI platform revenue acceleration.

events.title: RBA rate decision
events.why_it_matters: The RBA is expected to hold, but its tone matters for AUD and Australian miners exposed to China demand.
events.what_to_watch: Statement language on inflation and any hint of a 2027 cut.

events.title: Fed's Goolsbee speech
events.why_it_matters: Goolsbee is a 2026 voter; his comments after the hold will be parsed for the December hike debate.
events.what_to_watch: Any explicit signal on whether the Fed is done or still leaning hawkish.

top_risks: Iran/Hormuz escalation pushing Brent above $120 and reviving global inflation.
October CPI surprising to the upside and forcing a December Fed hike.
A contested or delayed US midterm result rattling already-edgy markets.
Legal and retaliatory chaos from the new 15% global tariff regime.
A weak Apple or AMD guide that cracks the AI/mega-cap leadership trade.
top_opportunities: Apple earnings beat and strong iPhone guidance stabilizing mega-cap tech.
OPEC+ surprise supply restraint lifting energy equities further.
Copper supply squeeze from Teck strike supporting miners.
Clear midterm outcome removing a political uncertainty premium.
Anthropic IPO successfully pricing and validating the AI ecosystem.
summary: Markets enter the final days before the US midterms with the Fed on hold but not done, inflation still sticky at 3.6% PCE, Brent above $115 on Hormuz risk, and a chaotic tariff reset after the Supreme Court struck down IEEPA duties. The coming week is dominated by mega-cap earnings (Apple, AMD, Qualcomm), the midterm election, US CPI and payrolls, and OPEC+; China's plenum delivered no major stimulus, leaving global cyclicals reliant on trade and inventory data. The main tension is between a market pricing a benign pause and a data-dependent path that could still force a December hike.
